calculationEntry.alt: The installed Plan a gift-kit commitment workflow is version 2.3.0 and offers Start analysis.
calculationEntry.caption: Start a new analysis from the installed collection. Existing saved reviews retain their exact releases.

calculationInputs.alt: A supplied one-day gift-kit case shows 120 kits, a $600 expense boundary and Calculate beside a pending Decision summary.
calculationInputs.caption: Leah checks the supplied commitment in Forms. Calculate assesses the evidence and complete correction options in dependency order.

calculationSummary.alt: The concise Decision summary prefers the $300 internal complete correction, ready at minute 40, and compares all five supplied packages.
calculationSummary.caption: The default report leads with the supported response and the decisive condition for each package. Complete evidence, work and requirements remain available separately.

ampleSummary.alt: With a full day available, the same cost-first workflow prefers the $300 internal complete correction at minute 40.
ampleSummary.caption: Full day: the $300 complete correction fits and costs less than the confirmed external package.

calculationEvidence.alt: The Supporting reports Evidence view identifies the printed-code and wrong-destination faults supported by the scoped observations.
calculationEvidence.caption: Evidence establishes what the complete correction must address. A successful old checkout does not verify the corrected kits.

calculationPlanning.alt: The complete-arrangements supporting report retains costs, handoff timing and conditions for all five supplied correction packages.
calculationPlanning.caption: Inspect the complete package when the summary raises a question. Choosing an inspection target changes neither the recommendation nor the recorded case.

calculationProcess.alt: The complete gift-kit Decision process graph connects fault evidence to complete correction packages and available responses, with current-case paths and reassessment arrows.
calculationProcess.caption: The gift-kit graph connects the supported faults to complete corrections and the responses available to Leah. The paths apply to the recorded one-day case; they do not release the kits.

calculationDependencies.alt: Calculation dependencies shows the evidence result feeding the gift-kit planning assessment and the resulting summary.
calculationDependencies.caption: This map explains how the supporting assessments connect. Opening it does not calculate or accept a result.

urgentSummary.alt: With thirty minutes remaining, the same cost-first workflow supports the confirmed $400 external correction, finishing at minute 1435.
urgentSummary.caption: Thirty minutes left: internal work finishes too late; the confirmed external package preserves five minutes before the same cutoff.

oldBookingSummary.alt: With the same urgent inputs but a booking for insert-2 instead of current insert-3, the Decision summary shows no supported complete correction.
oldBookingSummary.caption: A quote for fast work cannot replace a current booking. The old insert revision blocks external work while internal work still misses the deadline.

calculationPending.alt: The uncommitted $200 budget edit is flagged while the report continues to describe the last recorded $600 case.
calculationPending.caption: Draft input is separate from the recorded basis. Apply or discard the edit before recalculating.

calculationStale.alt: After the $200 limit is applied, the alternatives are marked stale and the earlier current correction proposal is withdrawn.
calculationStale.caption: Changed spending invalidates the planning basis. Recalculate reassesses the affected result; unchanged evidence remains current and the earlier planning finding remains historical.

calculationBlocked.alt: Under the $200 spending boundary, the completed calculation finds no supplied complete correction that meets the requirements.
calculationBlocked.caption: The $100 and $180 partial corrections leave faults unresolved; the $300 and $400 complete packages exceed the new limit.

calculationMobile.alt: The current gift-kit Decision summary retains the finding, complete comparison and supporting navigation on a phone.
calculationMobile.caption: The compact summary grows with the page; complete reports remain available when needed.

calculationProcessDetail.alt: A selected gift-kit feasibility question shows the current finding, its basis and the paths toward comparing supported complete corrections or revising the commitment.
calculationProcessDetail.caption: The selected question exposes the basis for comparing complete corrections. A supported package remains separate from carrying out its work and verifying the corrected kits.

timeWindow.title: The same campaign with a full day or thirty minutes remaining
timeWindow.sharedBasis: The same GIFT-120 case and Marketplace 2.3.0 workflow: 120 kits by minute 1,440, a $600 boundary, the same observations, package quotes, resources, permissions and current insert-3 booking. Ten minutes of fresh rehearsal are planned under the five-minute minimum.
timeWindow.change: Only the supplied current review time changes, from minute 0 to 1,410. Candidate starts follow that clock; no permission or booking is renewed.

panels.label: A full day remains
panels.explanation: Both complete packages fit. Leah can put forward the cheaper response without paying a deadline premium.

figure.alt: With a full day available, the same cost-first workflow prefers the $300 internal complete correction at minute 40.
figure.caption: Full day: the $300 complete correction fits and costs less than the confirmed external package.

panels.label: Thirty minutes remain
panels.explanation: Internal work now misses the original cutoff. The confirmed external package protects five minutes of remaining slack.

figure.alt: With thirty minutes remaining, the same cost-first workflow supports the confirmed $400 external correction, finishing at minute 1435.
figure.caption: Thirty minutes left: internal work finishes too late; the confirmed external package preserves five minutes before the same cutoff.

timeWindow.takeaway: The priority stays cost first. Changing the available time changes which complete correction meets the promise and whether the extra $100 is justified.

booking.title: The same urgent campaign with a current or old-insert booking
booking.sharedBasis: The same urgent GIFT-120 case, review at minute 1,410, deadline 1,440, $600 boundary, quotes, observations, permissions and availability under the same Marketplace 2.3.0 definition.
booking.change: Only the external booking’s insert revision changes: insert-3 versus insert-2. The campaign itself remains on insert-3.

panels.label: Booking covers the current insert
panels.explanation: The recorded booking supports this proposal. Responsible owners still authorize, perform and verify the work.

figure.alt: With thirty minutes remaining, the same cost-first workflow supports the confirmed $400 external correction, finishing at minute 1435.
figure.caption: Thirty minutes left: internal work finishes too late; the confirmed external package preserves five minutes before the same cutoff.

panels.label: Booking covers the previous insert
panels.explanation: Leah has a specific unsupported condition to resolve, rather than treating the fast quote as proof that the package can run.

figure.alt: With the same urgent inputs but a booking for insert-2 instead of current insert-3, the Decision summary shows no supported complete correction.
figure.caption: A quote for fast work cannot replace a current booking. The old insert revision blocks external work while internal work still misses the deadline.

booking.takeaway: Correct scope matters as much as quoted speed. Obtain a real current booking or another supported response; rewriting an old record would manufacture evidence.

calculationBudget.title: The same complete corrections under two spending boundaries
calculationBudget.sharedBasis: The same full-day GIFT-120 case and Marketplace 2.3.0 definition, with all quotes, observations, resources, permissions, current booking and ten planned rehearsal minutes unchanged.
calculationBudget.change: Only the expense boundary changes from $600 to $200. Planning becomes stale after Apply inputs and is reassessed by Recalculate.

panels.label: $600 available
panels.explanation: The cheaper complete package meets the promise, and the external package remains an alternative.

figure.alt: With a full day available, the same cost-first workflow prefers the $300 internal complete correction at minute 40.
figure.caption: Full day: the $300 complete correction fits and costs less than the confirmed external package.

panels.label: $200 available
panels.explanation: A finished calculation has established an operating blocker. Leah needs a changed authorization, a different complete quote or escalation.

figure.alt: Under the $200 spending boundary, the completed calculation finds no supplied complete correction that meets the requirements.
figure.caption: The $100 and $180 partial corrections leave faults unresolved; the $300 and $400 complete packages exceed the new limit.

calculationBudget.takeaway: A completed calculation can establish that none of the supplied responses fits. It does not waive the recorded spending requirement.
